channel.title: Honolulu Civil Beat - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Honolulu Civil Beat (civilbeat.org)

item.title: Where Are Honolulu’s Wāhine Lifeguards? 19 Out Of 20 Are Men
item.description: Hawaiʻi has some of the lowest rates of female lifeguards in the country. As more women surfers claim a spot in the lineup, there's hope that might change.

item.title: String Of ‘Devastating’ Suicides In Hawaiʻi Prisons Continues
item.description: Corrections officials are asking for millions of dollars this year to hire dozens of health care workers to improve mental health services inside.

item.title: Makana Eyre: New Hawaiʻi Novels Bring The State To Life Through Many Genres
item.description: Recent books about Hawaiʻi are changing how the outside world perceives us.

item.title: Bill Would Turn Kids Into Published Authors At Kalihi Schools
item.description: Lawmakers are pushing for the education department to create more hands-on and project-based learning opportunities for students.

item.title: Honolulu Police Officer Shoots Hālawa Man During Domestic Dispute
item.description: The man was wielding a knife and didn't stop approaching police after being shocked with a Taser, police chief said.

item.title: Photo Essay: Tournament Elevates The Historic Hawaiian Board Game Kōnane
item.description: The final match of the inaugural Ka Mākou Kōnane Championship Tournament was played on the Papamū Kūpuna, one of six known remaining wooden Kōnane boards in existence.

item.title: New Mauna Kea Authority Has Difficult Task Ahead — And Limited Time
item.description: University officials and some senators are concerned about the fate of astronomy on the mountain.

item.title: Word Row: Feb. 17
item.description: One word. Five letters. Six chances to solve. You can do it.

item.title: Divers Are Dying Near The Surface. Now There’s A Call For Safety Warnings
item.description: Freediving is one of the leading causes of fatal drownings for Hawaiʻi residents. Now lawmakers and safety advocates want labels on equipment — and more.

item.title: Mike Miske Case: Investigation Into Crime Syndicate May Not Be Over Yet
item.description: Recent court filings in the civil asset forfeiture case suggest that a criminal investigation may still be alive.
